title: Cohorted Launch Cadence Portfolio & Stability Insurance
creator: Miguel Santos
description:
Goal: Create a repeatable playbook and schedule for cohorted release trains (alpha/beta/gamma) that pairs capacity reservations with a lightweight 'stability insurance' pool. The playbook will reduce launch-day firefighting, improve predictability for Dedicated/Private capacity reservations, and give PMs a formal mechanism to hedge against unexpected latency/cost regressions during multi-surface rollouts (runtime/console/API).

Scope:
- Define cohort buckets and eligibility criteria (Alpha: internal, Beta: customers opted-in, Gamma: broad rollout).
- Design a launch portfolio cadence (week-of cadence, canary windows, rollback gates) that maps to capacity tokens and surge credits.
- Define the Stability Insurance pool: pre-authorized temporary capacity, rollback triggers, and communications flows.
- Integrate playbook with release calendar tool, ticket lifecycle states, and console runbook links.
- Provide SLAs for on-call escalation and runtime fallbacks (model variants, region fallback).

Success metrics:
- 30% reduction in cross-team launch incidents in first two quarters after adoption.
- <15 minute median time-to-decision for canary rollback during launches.
- Clear capacity booking usage: at least 80% of launches reserve appropriate cohort tokens.

Deliverables:
1) Cohort definitions and decision matrix (Alpha/Beta/Gamma).
2) Launch cadence calendar template and a per-train checklist.
3) Stability Insurance policy: budget, owner, approval flow, and runbook.
4) Integration docs: how to book tokens in the capacity ledger and link to release calendar.
5) Sample communications templates for go/no-go and post-launch status.

Constraints & trade-offs:
- Insurance pool increases short-term cost exposure; we recommend constraining it to X GPU-hours per quarter until telemetry validates reduced incident costs.
- Tight cohorting reduces reach early but enables safer iterations; product teams may request exceptions for strategic launches.
- We prioritize runtime and API launches first; Console-only surface upgrades scoped later in Q2 to limit cross-surface blast radius.

Plan / Timeline (next 4 weeks):
- Week 1: Draft cohort definitions + stability insurance policy (owner: PM).
- Week 2: Align with SRE and Capacity ops; prototype token booking in capacity ledger.
- Week 3: Run two dry-run launches (internal alpha, then beta shadow). Capture metrics.
- Week 4: Finalize playbook, add runbook to Console docs, and publish calendar templates.

Open questions:
- Exact GPU-hour cap for the insurance pool (proposal: 200 GPU-hours qtr for pilot).
- Approval baton: who can approve an insurance draw (PM + SRE on-call + capacity ops).
- How to bill insurance usage back to product teams (central fund vs. chargeback).
